did_you_know.text: Did you know? David prepared a special place for the ark of God in the City of David: he set up a tent for it so that the ark would be in its appointed place.

Did you know? After the failure of the first attempt to bring up the ark, David decreed that the Levites should carry the ark, because, as he said, the LORD had chosen them to carry the ark and minister before Him forever.

Did you know? David gathered the families of the Levites for the procession bringing up the ark, and the chapter lists the family heads and the number of their relatives: the families of Kohath, Merari, Gershom, Elizaphan, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Did you know? David instructed the heads of the Levitical families to consecrate themselves—that is, to prepare themselves properly, both spiritually and practically, before carrying the ark.

Did you know? David explained that the trouble that had struck them during the previous attempt was because they had not sought the ark according to the proper order; in other words, they had not acted according to the procedure they had been commanded to follow.
Did you know? The Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders using the poles, exactly as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD.
Did you know? Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed as the leaders of the musicians: Heman was from the family of Kohath, Asaph from the family of Gershom, and Ethan from the family of Merari.
Did you know? Chenaniah was appointed as the leader of the Levites in carrying the burden, and the text notes that he was knowledgeable and skilled in this responsibility.
Did you know? When the Levites successfully carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD with God's help, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
Did you know? When the ark of the covenant of the LORD arrived in the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul saw David leaping and celebrating from the window, and she despised him in her heart.
